div.div: مُفْحَمٌ [pass. part. n. of 4, q. v.]: i. q. عَيِىٌّ [app. as meaning Unable to express what he would say]; (K, TA;) because his face becomes black from anger, like فَحْم [i. e. charcoal]. (TA.) One unable to utter verse, or poetry. (S, * K.) And A poet who will not [or cannot] answer, or reply to, him who contends with him in satirizing. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
